name: NLnet Labs (Unbound, NSD)
description: Non-profit developer of DNS and routing software including Unbound, NSD, ldns and Routinator.
summary: NLnet Labs requires all code and documentation contributions to be authored by humans and does not accept LLM-generated content, though LLMs may be used for research, linting, analysis and reviewing your own work if you stay responsible for the output. LLM use when opening issues, sending vulnerability reports or posting on the forum must be disclosed, PR descriptions must be in your own words, and machine translation of your messages is discouraged.

evidence.quote: We require all code and documentation contributions to be authored by a human. You must not include content generated by LLMs or other probabilistic tools.
We do not accept LLM-generated contributions. Any code you submit cannot be generated by an LLM.
Your use of LLMs for linting, analysis or review is permitted under this policy. However, you remain responsible for the output of an LLM.
If an LLM assists you in finding or analysing an issue, you remain responsible to understand and verify the correctness of the information you share with us.
We want to interact with humans, not with LLMs. In your interactions with us, be respectful of our time, and disclose the use of an LLM.
This includes opening issues, sending vulnerability reports, and posting on our community forum.
Your use of LLMs for linting, analysis or review is permitted under this policy. However, you remain responsible for the output of an LLM.
If an LLM assists you in finding or analysing an issue, you remain responsible to understand and verify the correctness of the information you share with us.
To comply with this policy, after the LLM finds an issue, you as the human contributor verify the issue and the estimated severity.
As an exception to this rule, a suggested fix generated by an LLM as part of a vulnerability or bug report may be included, because it can help pinpoint the underlying issue during triage.
We accept reports of vulnerabilities found with LLMs. With your report, you can include an LLM suggested fix to help us pinpoint the issue.
Then, when you send a report to sep@nlnetlabs.nl you must disclose the use of an LLM.
When you open a PR, use your own words and be concise in the PR description.
We want to interact with humans, not with LLMs. In your interactions with us, be respectful of our time, and disclose the use of an LLM.
This includes opening issues, sending vulnerability reports, and posting on our community forum.

Translation can be helpful if English is not your native language. If you use machine translation when communicating with us, we encourage you to disclose such use to us so that both sides are aware of possible miscommunication as a result of mistranslation.
Alternatively, you could also write in your native language if you cannot assess the correctness of the translation.
Use of LLM translation is discouraged based on their generative attributes that would most likely confuse rather than ease the discussion.
